description: A Nova Gazeta report published February 23 says MEA members at the Faculty of Social Sciences, Agostinho Neto University, were detained while attempting to protest fee increases; it says the intended protest would be on campus and cites at least nine detentions from social media, but reports no total attendance and does not establish that a public gathering of 50 or more assembled. Angola24Horas and a Voz de Angola archive carry closely overlapping text; their written-origin relationship is unresolved. The opened Lusa/VerAngola S054 article dated February 22 also frames the action as an attempt to demonstrate on campus, says at least nine detentions were reported on social media and that police clarification was deferred; neither it nor Nova Gazeta S036 reports total turnout or verifies a 50+ assembly. Lusa/VerAngola and Nova Gazeta are differently attributed reports but both relay the MEA note; independent eyewitness corroboration is not established.
required_followup: Seek dated first-person, university, police, photo/video or other contemporary evidence showing whether a public assembly occurred, its total attendance, and the timing of detentions relative to any gathering. Keep null/pending until a 50+ physical assembly is established.

description: Novo Jornal body says police detained seven Cabinda activists, mostly organizers, near the Portuguese Embassy in Luanda on February 1 and later released them in Viana; the action was intended, but no total crowd size or confirmed 50+ assembly is established. Other search results report six detentions. The stated demand principally asks Portugal to take the Cabinda question to international forums, while the article also reports a demand for release of Cabinda political prisoners; direct domestic-state demand remains mixed. DW body is held because the global guard records a previous robots restriction on that publisher.
required_followup: Find accessible contemporaneous evidence establishing total attendance and whether a 50+ public assembly formed before arrests; clarify whether demands directly addressed Angola’s government as well as Portugal/international bodies. Do not use the blocked DW body or any copy/mirror; keep the lead outside events unless the eligibility criteria are supported.

description: E001 meets the reported size threshold, but exact location/route and physical end remain unresolved. S004 and S009 (same Novo Jornal publisher) place the intended route toward 1º de Maio; S004 quotes Largo da Independência; VOA S015 describes a Cemitério Sant’Ana assembly and Presidential Palace route. S004 explicitly attributes police gunfire and two leg wounds, while S009 only says shots were heard; the same-publisher reports are not independent corroboration. A later UESB thesis was opened only for a limited passage: it repeats a February 4 organizer leg-shot claim and footnote 108 points to an Amnesty Portugal campaign page. The derivative passage does not identify the organizer or establish event identity, is quarantined and is not used as E001 event/casualty evidence, and no footnote-page request was made. No captured report establishes a death or full physical end.
required_followup: Clarify site/route, seek independent contemporaneous or medical/court evidence identifying any injured people and whether any later source establishes a death, and find explicit evidence of when the assembly physically ended. E001 shootings=yes rests only on S004’s explicit National Police attribution; do not use the derivative UESB passage as confirmation, infer a death, or set an end date without closure evidence.

description: The non-exhaustive open-web pass used Portuguese and English and retained one French Cabinda communiqué. It did not systematically search Kimbundu, Umbundu, Kikongo or other regional/community-language archives, and provincial coverage outside Luanda/Cabinda is uneven. Searches across weekly windows and general labor, health, education and public-service terms do not establish that no other qualifying event occurred.
required_followup: Search local-language and province-specific media/archive collections with competent language review when available; continue sector-specific discovery. Keep this a coverage gap, not a zero-event finding.
